mcat_description.short: Conservatories are glazed room extensions — structures with glass or polycarbonate roofs and largely transparent walls — attached to or built adjacent to residential and commercial buildings to create sunlit enclosed living or working spaces. They are sold as custom-designed, site-installed structures with aluminium, uPVC, steel, or timber frames.
mcat_description.long: A conservatory is a glazed structural extension featuring a predominantly glass or polycarbonate roof and transparent or semi-transparent walls, designed to bring natural light into an enclosed habitable space while providing weather protection. In the Indian market, conservatories are most commonly supplied as custom-fabricated aluminium or uPVC-framed glass rooms installed on terraces, balconies, rooftops, and garden areas of residential villas, farmhouses, hotels, and commercial properties. Frame materials include aluminium alloy, uPVC, mild steel, and hardwood, while glazing options span tempered glass, laminated safety glass, insulated double-glazed units, polycarbonate sheets, and low-emissivity coated glass. Conservatories are sold as supply-and-install services quoted per square foot of built-up area, with full customisation of dimensions, roof style, frame colour, glazing type, and door configuration.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, conservatories are primarily sold as custom-designed, site-installed glass room extensions for residential terraces, balconies, and garden areas — commonly called 'glass rooms' by Indian buyers rather than 'conservatories.' The dominant construction uses aluminium alloy or uPVC frames with tempered or laminated safety glass roofs and walls, with polycarbonate sheet roofing as a lighter and more economical alternative. Key frame material options observed across Indian suppliers include aluminium, uPVC, mild steel, and wood, with glazing types spanning tempered glass, double-glazed insulated units, and polycarbonate. The broader Indian prefabricated buildings market is growing at approximately 7–8% CAGR (sources: Mordor Intelligence, IMARC Group), with demand for glass and composite-skin structures rising in Tier-I residential and commercial segments. Conservatories in India serve residential (villas, farmhouses, independent homes), hospitality (hotels, resorts, restaurants), and commercial (showrooms, cafés) buyers. The term 'glass room' is the dominant buyer-side vocabulary in India, while 'conservatory' is used more by sellers and in formal product listings. Cast iron conservatories represent a niche heritage/ornamental sub-segment. Pricing is quoted per sq ft of built-up area; all structures are custom-fabricated and site-installed.
